extracted.intended_audience: owners/operators of stationary combustion turbine EGUs, state and federal regulators, industry stakeholders
extracted.subtask_description: Preamble and regulatory text explaining New Source Performance Standards (40 CFR part 60, subparts TTTT and TTTTa) for new and reconstructed stationary combustion turbine electric generating units, including applicability, subcategorization, BSER determinations, exemptions, and compliance timing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability criteria for affected EGUs
rubrics_metrics.description: To be considered an affected EGU under the NSPS, the stationary combustion turbine must: (1) be capable of combusting more than 250 MMBtu/h (260 gigajoules per hour (GJ/h)) of heat input of fossil fuel (either alone or in combination with any other fuel); and (2) serve a generator capable of supplying more than 25 MW net to a utility distribution system (i.e., for sale to the grid).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are the baseline criteria for coverage under 40 CFR part 60, subparts TTTT and TTTTa. See also specified applicability exemptions that may exclude some units that otherwise meet these thresholds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability exemptions (types of EGUs exempted)
rubrics_metrics.description: Exemptions include: (1) non-fossil fuel-fired units subject to a federally enforceable permit limiting fossil fuel use to 10 percent or less of annual heat input; (2) CHP units subject to a federally enforceable permit limiting annual net electric sales to no more than either the unit's design efficiency multiplied by its potential electric output, or 219,000 MWh, whichever is greater; (3) stationary combustion turbines not physically capable of combusting natural gas (e.g., not connected to a natural gas pipeline); (4) utility boilers and IGCC units that have always been subject to a federally enforceable permit limiting annual net electric sales to one-third or less of potential output or limiting annual electric sales to 219,000 MWh or less; (5) municipal waste combustors subject to 40 CFR part 60, subpart Eb; (6) commercial or industrial solid waste incineration units subject to 40 CFR part 60, subpart CCCC; and (7) certain projects under development as discussed in the 2015 NSPS preamble.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These exemptions are applied to avoid regulating units that were intended to be outside the fossil-fuel EGU NSPS. The text explains how permit conditions and historic sales can affect exemption status; see separate entry on electric sales permit revision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subcategorization and definitions (low load / intermediate load / base load; elimination of multi-fuel subcategory)
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA creates three subcategories for stationary combustion turbines used in the power sector: low load (peaking units; low annual capacity factors; quick start and ramp ability, lower capital cost and lower efficiency), intermediate load (cycling/load-following; vary generation; either highly efficient simple cycle or flexible fast-start combined cycle may be appropriate), and base load (designed to operate for extended periods at high loads; typically high-efficiency combined cycle). The multi-fuel-fired subcategory is eliminated and non-base load turbines are binned into low load and intermediate load; a capacity factor threshold for base load turbines is established.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subcategory membership is determined by intended role, annual capacity factor/operation profile and design characteristics. The definition of base/intermediate/low load drives which BSER and standard of performance apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: BSER for low load combustion turbines
rubrics_metrics.description: For low load combustion turbines, the EPA is finalizing a determination that the use of lower-emitting fuels is the appropriate Best System of Emission Reduction (BSER).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The BSER determination leads to standards of performance for low load turbines that are based on fuel-selection / fuel-emissions characteristics rather than efficiency upgrades or CCS.

rubrics_metrics.name: BSER for intermediate load combustion turbines
rubrics_metrics.description: For intermediate load combustion turbines, the EPA is finalizing a determination that highly efficient simple cycle generation is the appropriate BSER.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standards of performance for intermediate load units reflect achievable higher-efficiency simple cycle designs (and consideration of flexible fast-start combined cycle vs. simple cycle given intended operation).

rubrics_metrics.name: BSER for base load combustion turbines (two-component, phased)
rubrics_metrics.description: For base load combustion turbines, the EPA is finalizing a BSER that includes two components corresponding to a two-phase standard of performance: (Phase 1, immediate compliance) highly efficient generation based on the performance of a highly efficient combined cycle turbine; and (Phase 2, compliance date January 1, 2032) the use of CCS with a 90 percent capture rate, along with continued use of highly efficient generation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Both phase 1 and phase 2 standards of performance apply to new and reconstructed sources that commence construction or reconstruction after May 23, 2023. The EPA refers to the phase 1 or phase 2 standards when discussing these components.

rubrics_metrics.name: Phase timing and applicability for subpart TTTTa (construction/reconstruction date)
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards of performance apply to EGUs that commence construction or reconstruction after the date of proposal of this rule—May 23, 2023. EGUs that commenced construction after the proposal for the 2015 NSPS and by May 23, 2023, remain subject to the 2015 standards. A reconstruction can render an existing source a 'new source' under NSPS general provisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This sets the regulatory effective timeframe for which subpart TTTTa applies and clarifies that reconstruction triggers new-source treatment for applicability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Geographic variation for non-contiguous and non-continental areas
rubrics_metrics.description: Owners/operators of combustion turbines in non-contiguous and non-continental areas (Alaska, Hawaii, Virgin Islands, Guam, American Samoa, Puerto Rico, Northern Mariana Islands) are subject only to the initial BSER component (phase 1). Phase-2 (CCS-based numerical standards effective 2032) will not apply in these areas in this final rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA considered comment and local conditions; the Agency retains authority to amend this decision in future rulemakings. EPA notes limited current new turbine activity in Alaska and Hawaii.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revision to non-fossil fuel-fired EGU definition (combusting → deriving; include non-combustion heat input)
rubrics_metrics.description: The EPA is amending the non-fossil applicability exemption language from EGUs capable of 'combusting 50 percent or more non-fossil fuel' to EGUs capable of 'deriving 50 percent or more of the heat input from non-fossil fuel at the base load rating.' The definition of base load rating is also amended to include the heat input from non-combustion sources (e.g., solar thermal).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This change ensures facilities that primarily derive energy from non-combustion sources (like solar thermal with limited natural gas backup) are not inappropriately covered, and counting 'derived' heat input rather than only combustion aligns coverage with original intent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Industrial EGU exemption where >50% heat input derived from industrial process
rubrics_metrics.description: The EPA is amending the applicability provision to exempt EGUs where greater than 50 percent of the heat input is derived from an industrial process that does not produce any electrical or mechanical output or useful thermal output that is used outside the affected EGU.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This avoids covering industrial projects that add useful electric output with little additional environmental impact and would otherwise incur compliance burden without environmental benefit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Electric sales exemption permit requirement revision (removal of 'always been')
rubrics_metrics.description: The EPA is revising the electric sales exemption language to delete the word 'always been' — the exemption will read: 'annual net electric sales have never exceeded one-third of its potential electric output or 219,000 MWh, whichever is greater, and is subject to a federally enforceable permit limiting annual net electric sales to one-third or less of their potential electric output ... or limiting annual electric sales to 219,000 MWh or less.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This allows an owner/operator of an existing industrial EGU to provide evidence that the facility has never sold electricity in excess of the threshold and to modify their permit to limit future sales, avoiding unintended coverage of units that never actually sold above the threshold.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determination of design efficiency — alternative methods and Administrator approval
rubrics_metrics.description: Because original design-efficiency documentation may be unavailable or irrelevant for existing EGUs, EPA allows alternative methods to demonstrate design efficiency as approved by the Administrator on a case-by-case basis. Administrator's discretion can extend to other ASME or ISO methods as well as operating data. EPA is changing the applicability of paragraph 60.8(b) in table 3 to 'yes' to allow Administrator approval of alternatives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Owners/operators may petition in writing for approval of an alternate method. This reduces compliance burden where original test/guarantee records no longer exist or reflect current configurations.

rubrics_metrics.name: CHP net electric sales calculation changes (eliminate 20% threshold and clarify subtraction of host purchased power)
rubrics_metrics.description: For subpart TTTTa, EPA is eliminating the restriction that CHP units produce at least 20.0 percent electrical or mechanical output to qualify for the CHP-specific method of calculating net electric sales and net energy output. The existing approach allows subtraction of purchased power of the thermal host facility when determining net electric sales; EPA notes ambiguity in how third-party CHPs subtract host facility electricity under the 2015 language.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Removing the 20% threshold makes the CHP-specific calculation method available to more CHP configurations; EPA intends to clarify net electric sales calculation so third-party developers and host-owned CHPs are treated consistently.
